questions.text: Passenger Non-Discrimination: Equal service: (1) Policy against discrimination (race, gender, disability); (2) Monitoring of trip refusals (by destination); (3) Accessibility features (wheelchair-accessible vehicles); (4) Service to 'unsafe' areas; (5) Pricing fairness (no redlining); (6) Complaint mechanism for discrimination; (7) Driver training on inclusion.
questions.evidence_required: Non-discrimination policy, Trip refusal analysis, Accessibility vehicle count
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drivers often refuse trips to 'slum' areas or at night. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles are rare. Discrimination by tribe/accent occurs.

questions.text: Driver Fair Treatment: Algorithmic fairness: (1) Fair allocation of trips (no favoritism); (2) Transparent deactivation criteria; (3) Appeal process for penalties; (4) Protection from false passenger accusations; (5) Fair rating system (outlier removal); (6) Equal access to incentives; (7) Bias testing of algorithms.
questions.evidence_required: Trip allocation algorithm, Deactivation appeal logs, Rating fairness analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Drivers suspect favoritism (better trips to 'preferred' drivers). False accusations (theft, harassment) can destroy livelihoods.

questions.text: Environmental Impact Management: Green transport: (1) Emissions tracking (carbon footprint); (2) Incentives for electric/hybrid vehicles; (3) Route optimization for fuel efficiency; (4) Carpooling/shared rides promotion; (5) Offset programs (tree planting); (6) Reporting on environmental impact; (7) Transition plan to clean energy.
questions.evidence_required: Carbon footprint reports, EV incentive programs, Offset initiatives
questions.africa_specific_notes: Air pollution is a major urban issue. EVs are expensive but growing (e.g., electric boda-bodas in Kenya). Carpooling reduces congestion.

questions.text: Traffic Congestion & Urban Impact: Responsible growth: (1) Congestion impact assessment; (2) Collaboration with city planners; (3) Support for public transport integration; (4) Peak hour demand management; (5) Parking compliance; (6) Noise pollution mitigation (boda-bodas); (7) Community engagement.
questions.evidence_required: Congestion studies, Public transport integration plans, Community feedback
questions.africa_specific_notes: Ride-hailing adds to congestion. Integration with matatus (minibuses) could help. Boda-bodas are noisy and chaotic.

questions.text: Pricing Ethics & Exploitation Prevention: Fair pricing: (1) Cap on surge pricing (during emergencies); (2) Transparency on dynamic pricing; (3) Protection of vulnerable users (elderly, disabled); (4) No predatory pricing (undercutting to monopolize); (5) Fair commission rates; (6) No hidden fees; (7) Regulatory compliance on pricing.
questions.evidence_required: Pricing policy, Surge cap documentation, Regulatory filings
questions.africa_specific_notes: Surge during emergencies (floods, protests) is seen as exploitative. Regulators have intervened (e.g., Kenya capping surge).

questions.text: Anti-Corruption & Bribery: Clean operations: (1) Policy against bribes (to police, regulators); (2) Reporting mechanism for bribery; (3) Training on anti-corruption; (4) Transparency in regulatory interactions; (5) Whistleblower protection; (6) Audit of payments to officials; (7) Collaboration with anti-corruption agencies.
questions.evidence_required: Anti-bribery policy, Training logs, Whistleblower reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Traffic police often demand bribes. Platforms must not facilitate this. Drivers need support to resist.

questions.text: Ethical Data Use: Responsible data practices: (1) No sale of user data to third parties; (2) Consent for secondary uses (research, marketing); (3) Anonymization for analytics; (4) Protection of sensitive data (health, political); (5) Transparency on government data requests; (6) Data minimization principle; (7) User control over data.
questions.evidence_required: Data ethics policy, Consent management system, Transparency reports
questions.africa_specific_notes: Location data is highly sensitive (can reveal political affiliations, religious sites). Government surveillance is a risk.

questions.text: Algorithmic Accountability: Fair algorithms: (1) Bias testing (gender, race, location); (2) Explainability of decisions (deactivation, pricing); (3) Human oversight of automated decisions; (4) Regular audits of algorithms; (5) Transparency on algorithm changes; (6) Redress for algorithmic harm; (7) Stakeholder input on algorithm design.
questions.evidence_required: Bias audit reports, Algorithm change logs, Redress mechanisms
questions.africa_specific_notes: Algorithms can perpetuate discrimination (e.g., avoiding certain neighborhoods). Transparency and accountability are essential.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Transport in SSA: Non-discrimination (destination, disability) is a major trust issue. Environmental impact is growing in importance. Ethical pricing (surge caps) is a regulatory flashpoint.
